355956.title: Yip's maximal subfield clique conjecture for generalized Paley graphs

scope_fidelity.mathdb_statement: d>1; q ≡ 1 (mod 2d) a power of prime p; r largest with d | (q-1)/(p^r-1); then F_{p^r} is a maximal clique in GP(q,d)=Cay(F_q^+, (F_q^*)^d).
scope_fidelity.primary_text: Identical to Yip, J. Algebraic Combin. 56(2) (2022) 323-333 = arXiv:2101.09652 Conjecture 1.4 (v2 read), and to arXiv:2209.00864 v2 / Algebr. Comb. 6(4) (2023) 901-905 Conjecture 1.1 (arXiv TeX and published ALCO TeX read). Asgarli-Yip arXiv:2106.01522 v2 / JCTA 192 (2022) restates it with the added clause 'F_{p^r} is a subfield of F_q', which is implied by d | (q-1)/(p^r-1) being an integer condition, so equivalent.
scope_fidelity.quantifiers: Universal over d, p, q; the refutation needs one admissible (q,d). q = 5^8, d = 3: q-1 = 390624 ≡ 0 (mod 6); admissible r ∈ {1} only, so r = 1 and the claim is 'F_5 is a maximal clique in GP(5^8,3)'.
scope_fidelity.metadata_note: MathDB status field is 'open'. Its references field carries a mis-attached quote ('Status: solved according to the source') which concerns the Peisert-graph analogue confirmed by Asgarli-Yip, not this conjecture. The statement text itself says the paper resolves it only 'under a sufficient-size hypothesis'.

ordinary_mathematics.script: scripts/yip_verify.py (own GF(5^8) arithmetic; no shared code); log logs/yip-verify.log; output checks/yip-verify.json; 1.9 s under 2 CPU / 6 GiB / 120 s caps
facts_verified: f = X^8+X^7+2X^6+2 is irreducible over F_5 (X has Frobenius orbit length 8)
-1 and all of F_5^* are cubes (F_5 is a clique; graph undirected)
x = 2θ+4θ^2+θ^3 ∉ F_5 and x-a is a nonzero cube for a = 0..4 (direct exponentiation (x-a)^((q-1)/3) = 1)
F_5 ⊕ xF_5 is a 25-clique (all 24 nonzero a+bx are cubes), as predicted by Yip's Lemma 2.1 (JACO 2022)
generators of F_25^* and F_625^* are non-cubes, so F_5 is also a maximal SUBFIELD clique (Theorem 1.2's hypothesis structure, minus q>(n-1)^2)
exhaustive: exactly 960 extension vertices, all of degree 8 over F_5 (log-table count, consistent with direct exponentiation)
ordinary_mathematics.consistency_with_source_computations: No extension vertex lies in F_625; since GP(5^8,3) restricted to F_625 is GP(625,3) (626 ≡ 2 mod 3), this agrees with Yip's reported SageMath verification for n ≤ 5 (here n = 4, q = 5). The counterexample needs n = 8, outside both Yip's checks (n ≤ 5; n = 6 with q ≤ 17) and Theorem 1.2 (5 ≤ (8-1)^2 = 49). No theorem in the read literature is contradicted (Prop. cliquenumber2 of arXiv:2304.13213 needs q < d|K|(|K|+1) = 90, false here).

novelty.basis: All primary follow-ups by the conjecture's author treat it as confirmed or proved within range; the 2025 DCC paper restates it as proved; no registry entry; web search negative.

reasons: Refutes, in exact universal scope, a published conjecture (JACO 2022, Conj. 1.4) that its author's follow-up (ALCO 2023) announces as 'confirmed'/'resolved' and that a later published paper (DCC 2025) restates as proved without qualification; this corrects the published record, not a wording slip.

Also refutes the explicit remark-conjecture of ALCO 2023 that the hypothesis q > (n-1)^2 can be dropped from Theorem 1.2 (F_5 is a maximal subfield clique that is not a maximal clique), showing that some size hypothesis is genuinely necessary for GP, the case the source distinguished from GP*, where it exhibited failures.

Not a routine corollary: no known theorem implies it; the source's own exhaustive checks (n ≤ 5; n = 6, q ≤ 17) did not find it; it first occurs at n = 8 with q = 390625, outside the obvious first tests. The author's sweep (q ≤ 5·10^6, 219 open-range cases) found only this one.

Not a parameter instance in the excluded sense: a single admissible (q,d) is a complete negative resolution of the universal conjecture; not a domain/endpoint correction (the hypotheses q ≡ 1 mod 2d, d>1 hold literally).
Mathematical content beyond the finite check: it gives ω(GP(5^8,3)) ≥ 25 via a 2-dimensional F_5-subspace clique, contradicting the 'tempting' ω = |K| heuristic of DCC 2025.
adversarial_points_considered: The existence of counterexamples for the GP* analogue (ALCO remark) makes a GP failure plausible a posteriori; the source nonetheless conjectured the opposite for GP specifically.

Theorem 1.2 covers p^r > (n-1)^2, i.e. most large-subfield cases; the counterexample lives in the regime the source admitted was unproven. This bounds but does not remove significance, because the source asserted the unrestricted conjecture and claimed it confirmed.
The q ≤ 5·10^6 sweep and 'only failure' claim is author diagnostic data, not part of the result; I re-verified only (5^8,3).

355956.recommendation: Eligible for root acceptance on source fidelity, novelty (bounded) and significance. Present the paper as a counterexample to Yip's Conjecture 1.4 (= ALCO Conj. 1.1) and to the ALCO remark-conjecture, noting explicitly that Theorem 1.2 is not contradicted (5 ≤ 49) and that the published abstract's 'confirms' and the DCC 2025 restatement overstate what was proved. Cite the 25-clique F_5 ⊕ xF_5.

355701.title: Partial converse for monochromatic triangles in symmetric v3 configurations

scope_fidelity.verdict: FAITHFUL, with a reading ambiguity of 'maximal'
scope_fidelity.mathdb_statement: Symmetric v3 configuration containing a maximal set of mutually intersecting lines of size i; if the minimum number of monochromatic triangles over line 2-colourings is non-zero then i > 4.
scope_fidelity.primary_text: Verbatim identical in arXiv:2208.06912 v1 (2022-08-14; then titled 'Minimum numbers of monochromatic triangles in line 2-colorings of v3 configurations of points and lines'), v2 (2024-04-26) and EJGTA 11(2) 2023, DOI 10.5614/ejgta.2023.11.2.8, Conjecture 1 (received 25 July 2022, revised 11 June 2023, accepted 6 August 2023). Definitions §2.2: configurations purely combinatorial; no connectivity requirement; triangle Def. 4.1 (three points pairwise on lines avoiding the third point).
scope_fidelity.reading: Source context ('Pappus's configuration contains maximally three intersecting lines and the Möbius-Kantor four') indicates i = maximum size (clique number of the line-intersection graph). The inclusion-maximal reading is literally allowed by the wording.
source_defects: Second example (claimed max 5 intersecting lines, min 1, cited as showing the converse of Thm 6.1 fails) is not a v3 configuration: point 1 lies on 4 lines (identical in v1, v2, EJGTA).

The 'Young configuration' (Fig. 7, Thm 4.2) is, from the figure, the 3x3 grid with rows, columns, diagonals and broken diagonals, i.e. AG(2,3) = Hesse (9_4,12_3): each point lies on 4 lines, so it is not a symmetric v3 configuration either, despite the section heading. Its min 0 claim is correct for that object but irrelevant to v3.

endpoint_split.conjectureInclusion_false: ZERO independent weight. Under the inclusion-maximal reading, the conjecture is already refuted by the source's own Example (connected sum of two Fano planes): min = 4 (source's GAP claim, reconfirmed here) and it has inclusion-maximal intersecting sets of sizes 3, 5 and 6. Also refuted by the disconnected Fano ⊔ Pappus (min 4, inclusion-maximal size 3), which the source's definition admits. Reading/wording triviality.
endpoint_split.conjectureMaximum_false: The only substantive endpoint. Resolves the conjecture under its natural reading.

reasons_for_hold: The counterexample is an explicit standard object: one of the only three 9_3 configurations, a classical catalogue (Hilbert-Cohn-Vossen; Grünbaum 2009 §2.2). v3 configurations exist only for n ≥ 7; n = 7 (Fano, max 7) and n = 8 (Möbius-Kantor, min 0, unique) cannot refute, so the counterexample sits at the smallest possible order, and among the two 9_3 configurations the source did not check. One of these two refutes.

It is obtained by running the source's own published GAP procedure on that catalogue entry (512 colourings). Unlike the conference-matrix precedent (conference-significance-adjudication-r2, where first-test and neglect claims were judged unestablished), here the first-test claim is concretely established: the next catalogue entry after the source's own list refutes it.

The conjecture's evidential basis in the source is defective: its only claimed witness that the converse of Thm 6.1 fails is not a v3 configuration, and its 'Young' example is not v3. Open status reflects zero engagement (0 citations), not difficulty.

No structural content: no infinite connected family, no characterisation of when min > 0 at max intersecting size 4; infinitude is trivial via disjoint unions because the source allows disconnected configurations.
significance.strongest_case_for: Exact-scope negative resolution of a journal-published conjecture under its natural reading, with a literal Lean endpoint, no prior report, and the smallest possible counterexample. Under the conference-r2 'minimum threshold' standard (ease/runtime/no infinite theorem are not written exclusions), a QUALIFIED_PASS restricted to conjectureMaximum_false is defensible.
significance.why_hold_not_fail: Not a known theorem, public refutation, corollary, endpoint correction or parameter instance in the written sense. The deciding question, whether evaluating the next entry of a classical finite catalogue with the source's own code is 'routine', is a campaign-standard judgment reserved to root.
significance.would_change_verdict: Toward PASS: a structural theorem (e.g. an infinite family of CONNECTED v3 configurations with max intersecting size 4 and min > 0, or a characterisation at size 4). Toward FAIL: root ruling that a refutation by an unmodified classical catalogue object, via the source's own algorithm, is routine.

355701.recommendation: Do not count on present evidence; HOLD for root significance adjudication. If root applies the conference-r2 minimum-threshold precedent and counts it, credit scope must be the maximum reading only (conjectureMaximum_false). conjectureInclusion_false must carry no weight. The paper must disclose that (i) it is the aut-order-9 member of the three classical 9_3 configurations, (ii) the inclusion reading falls to the source's own Fano connected sum, and (iii) the source's second example and Young configuration are not v3.
limitations: Grünbaum §2.2 not re-read (label (9_3)_2 asserted from standard knowledge; the computational facts are my own)
